analysis: Examined the SSD prefix-cache eviction refactor (T-041, TB-007, A-001). SSDBlockIndex.swift replaces the fully sorted oldestEntries() with a lazily produced binary-heap OldestFirstSnapshot (lines 167-225). The snapshot is copied under the index lock, and the heap is a correct min-heap: heapify via siftDown from count/2-1, next() pops the root and moves the last element to the top, and siftDown picks the smaller child. The comparator matches oldest() (lastAccess, then lexicographic tag bytes). withUnsafeBytes lexicographicallyPrecedes gives the same unsigned-byte ordering as Data's lexicographicallyPrecedes. Tags are unique, so the order is total. No change to the at-rest data format, HMAC naming, encryption, TTL or epoch handling, and no new data exposure. SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift (lines 13-21) now guards evictOldestEntry on isClosed and delegates to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, which is not supplied. The patch removes the base's early return on retired.externalChange, so external-removal and stop-pass behavior lives in the unseen helper. The docs claim that behavior is preserved: a closed store is never reopened, and reconciliation stops the pass. The isClosed guard strengthens the T-041 invariant that a closed or disowned store never performs removals. Remaining integration question: verify the SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest implementation. It should perform per-file removal only under the store removal lock and epoch ownership via retireIndexedEntries, never rotate the epoch, and not loop unboundedly. The SSDDiskBudget.enforce progress and blockedStores logic is unchanged and depends on evictOldestEntry returning 0 when the store is closed. The docs-only change to docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md line 375 is descriptive, and the threat model needs no update. No security regression identified. Deeper review is only needed for the unseen helper, as a low-priority completeness check.
